nodes.question: Where should the smoke test live and how is it triggered: a standalone script run by hand or npm script, a new job in deploy.yml (needs: deploy and deploy-api), a separate workflow_dispatch/workflow_run workflow, or a combination? 'Without deploying anything' rules out a deploy step but does not say which.
nodes.answer: Only two workflows exist: deploy.yml and release.yml. There is no dedicated smoke or post-deploy workflow. deploy.yml runs on push to main and on workflow_dispatch, which has one input, pulumi_refresh. The `deploy` job (bot) and `deploy-api` job (API) are separate, parallel jobs, and both use `environment: prod`. Each deploy job ends with its own curl retry loop on /_healthz, so health checks already live inside the deploy jobs. `deploy` does this at lines 213-227 and `deploy-api` at lines 350-364. Prod URLs are not hard-coded. The workflow reads them with `gcloud run describe ... status.url` after authenticating through Workload Identity (vars.PROD_WIF_PROVIDER and PROD_CI_SA_EMAIL). Prod secrets such as PROD_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, PROD_TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and PROD_API_SHARED_SECRET are available only through `environment: prod`. The bot exposes POST /push in apps/bot/src/server.ts. The API serves GET /daily-push through handleDailyPush, imported in api-server.ts. The root package.json has npm scripts such as check:phone (which runs a scripts/*.mjs file) and models:prices. Standalone checks under scripts/ are an existing pattern, for example scripts/check-web-node-builtins.mjs, which deploy.yml runs with `node`. No smoke script exists for this ticket. TODO.md lists the ticket with an empty 'Coding tasks' section and no placement guidance.

nodes.question: What should the webhook config check assert? The bot can call Telegram getWebhookInfo with PROD_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and compare url to https://bot.postanki.ilya.online/telegram. It could also check pending_update_count and last_error_message. Nothing in the repo says which fields should fail the test, and the production webhook path and host are not confirmed in code I read.
nodes.quote: checks the Telegram bot webhook config
nodes.answer: The bot's webhook route is POST /telegram; any other method or path is rejected by that check. The bot host in prod is bot.postanki.ilya.online. Infra defaults botDomain to it, the AWS Pulumi config comments name it as botHostname, and the deploy checklist says the bot moved to this subdomain. The deploy checklist sets the webhook with `npm run set-webhook -w @post-anki/bot https://bot.postanki.ilya.online/telegram`. That makes the expected webhook URL https://bot.postanki.ilya.online/telegram. docs/ci-cd/gcp-setup.md gives a different set-webhook URL, https://postanki.ilya.online/telegram, on the root domain. It conflicts with .inbox/TODOS.md, which says the bot moved to the subdomain and the root domain now belongs to the web app. set-webhook.ts calls Telegram setWebhook and passes secret_token from TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. getWebhookInfo does not return the secret, so the test cannot check it there. The prod secrets PROD_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and PROD_TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET are documented as GitHub secrets. POST /push returns 401 when the Authorization header differs from `Bearer ${TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET}`. On success it returns 200 and then runs the daily push in the background. A smoke test that sends the correct bearer would therefore trigger a real push to the owner's Telegram chat. The bot has GET /_healthz, which returns 200 'ok'. The API's GET /daily-push is called by the bot's client as `${API_BASE_URL}/daily-push?mode=...`. It is also used by the web app, and its response is {push, question}. Nothing in the repo says which getWebhookInfo fields should fail the test. The code and docs only show the url being set, so pending_update_count and last_error_message have no documented thresholds.

nodes.question: What does 'bot /push auth' mean for pass criteria? Safest reading: no or wrong bearer gives 401. A valid-secret call would trigger a real Telegram push to the owner, so whether to send one (or only check 401) needs a decision.
nodes.answer: The bot's POST /push compares the Authorization header to `Bearer ${TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET}` and returns 401 with an empty body when it doesn't match, so a missing or wrong bearer is a safe, side-effect-free check. With a valid bearer, /push returns 200 immediately and then runs runDailyPush in the background. That job clears the owner's chat context and sends the day's question to OWNER_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID. A valid-secret call therefore causes a real Telegram message and a context reset. The bot has two other bearer-gated endpoints that mirror /push's auth: one returns 401 at line 194 and the other at line 219. Neither is named in the ticket. The secret that /push checks is the same value as the bot's TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The Cloud Scheduler job sends it as the bearer when it POSTs the bot's /push once a day. The scheduler job post-anki-daily-push targets `${botService.statuses[0].url}/push`. The API's GET /daily-push only returns a question and delivers nothing. The web app uses it as a pull, and the bot fetches from it. The existing manual post-deploy check for the daily push is to trigger the scheduler once and expect a Telegram message. This is a separate, delivering check.

nodes.question: What should the API GET /daily-push assertion cover: 401 without auth, 200 with the shared secret, and a response schema check (push, question, nudge keys)? A 200 may invoke an LLM and cost money, and may return nulls when there is nothing due.
Should the smoke test be a standalone script (an npm script run by hand), a job in deploy.yml, a separate workflow, or a combination? Nothing in the repo or wiki decides this.
nodes.answer: deploy.yml is the only prod deploy workflow. It triggers on push to main and on workflow_dispatch, and has jobs deploy (bot), deploy-api and an optional deploy-web. Each deploy job already ends with an in-workflow curl health-check step, for example 'Verify deployment health' for the bot and 'Verify API health' for the API. Verification steps are an established pattern in deploy.yml. The bot and API deploy as separate parallel jobs, both needing [test, infra, review-factory-gate]. A smoke test spanning bot and API would need its own job with needs: [deploy, deploy-api]. The prod environment secrets PROD_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, PROD_TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and PROD_API_SHARED_SECRET are available to jobs with environment: prod. The bot and API URLs are resolved with gcloud run describe using the WIF auth steps. The bot's POST /push requires the header 'Authorization: Bearer <TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET>'. The Telegram webhook uses the header x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token. The bot's POST /push compares the Authorization header with Bearer TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using secretsEqual. The API exposes GET /daily-push (route name dailyPush). The repo has a convention of standalone scripts in scripts/ (for example check-web-node-builtins.mjs, source-items-smoke.mjs). deploy.yml calls check-web-node-builtins.mjs directly with node. A smoke script in that folder would fit this pattern and could be run by hand or from CI. release.yml is a separate workflow triggered on push to main. It only publishes a GitHub release and builds the Mac app, so it is unrelated to prod verification.

Whether a smoke-test failure should fail or block the deploy workflow. It runs after the deploys, so it cannot prevent them; it can only turn the run red or trigger a rollback or alert.

Where a manual run gets the prod URLs and secrets (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN for the webhook config, TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET for /push auth). The script could read them from environment variables, and the person running it would supply the values. How the person holds those secrets locally is not documented.

The auth scheme of the API's GET /daily-push (shared secret, or none) and the expected webhook URL that getWebhookInfo should return were not read. I found no setWebhook or getWebhookInfo code in the repo.
